title: Joint voice-motion instructions constrained by historical counterpoint
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, SOURCE_ONLY, NOT SELECTED. Recover complete instructions about coordinated voices through a shared written code constrained simultaneously by melodic motion and harmonic intervals. No paired-voice Voynich target has been established; this raw proposal preserves a distinct functional system, not a musical identification.

design.source_observation: The primary-text edition ANO11TRA, Sequitur ars contratenoris, explicitly makes a contratenor choice depend on where discantus begins and whether tenor is low or high. It also prohibits two successive octaves while moving with tenor. These are linked state constraints, rather than an arbitrary note-name list.
design.source_access: Primary edition text returned in web search; complete edition/variant rules not yet collated. Do not silently substitute modern species-counterpoint rules.
design.candidate_reading: A whole passage describes simultaneous voice events; one global finite code must recover voice identity, relative motion, harmonic interval and prescribed response for every event. No per-event key, skipped instruction, flexible alignment or arbitrary initial melody.
design.incompatible_predictions: Two proposed interpretations giving the same individual pitch inventories can disagree about successive parallel octaves or which voice remains fixed. Freeze the historical rule variant and voice alignment first; a complete continuation must satisfy the same directional/harmonic constraints without key change.
design.positive_output: A complete recovered instruction and predicted continuation whose voice/motion/interval interpretation agrees across every surviving key, with absolute-pitch/transposition and voice-permutation ambiguities explicitly retained. Mere legal music does not identify a natural-language phrase.
design.minimum_test: Before target selection, collate one short complete primary worked counterpoint example and its written rule, then determine whether joint rule/example constraints identify the operational reading under a preregistered bounded channel. Target work requires an independently nominated paired-voice or explicit instruction/example manuscript structure; none currently exists. This is not authorization for an automatic control series.
principal_risks: No admitted manuscript observation presently identifies paired voices.
Many legal melodies and interchangeable encodings can satisfy the same counterpoint rules.
Treatise date, variant and exceptions require primary review; modern rules would be anachronistic.
design.duplicate_boundary: Bounded counterpoint search found no card; GDT902 exact solmization register is a different fixed-copy model and remains closed. This proposal concerns coupled voice motion, not a relaxed solmization code. It does not reopen GDT906/911.
